scope: Portable host C fixed-period normalized millisecond clock owner, plus composition before the existing final gate. Not a target timer or full controller.
semantics: Configured period is an ordinary integer from 1 through 60000 milliseconds.
Python timestamp is an ordinary nonnegative integer; bool, float, negative and nonnumeric values are invalid_cycle_timestamp. Python retains its unbounded integer domain.

C timestamp/previous state domain is uint64 milliseconds with an explicit exact-valid tag. Decoder rejects rather than wraps values outside this domain. This is an explicit representability restriction, not a Python policy change.
First valid timestamp establishes the anchor at any nonnegative value, even if dt is invalid.
Duplicate/backward timestamps are nonmonotonic_cycle_timestamp and do not advance the prior anchor.
A forward gap unequal to the period is cycle_period_mismatch and does advance the anchor to that timestamp.
Ordinary finite dt must be within absolute 1e-12 seconds of period_ms/1000, with zero relative tolerance. Invalid dt is guard_period_mismatch unless a timestamp fault already owns precedence.
Valid forward timestamps advance the anchor even when the dt check fails. Restart does not reset the clock anchor.
Normalized now is the valid source timestamp even for backward/gapped samples; malformed timestamps normalize to absent.
No timestamp wrapping, clamping, float conversion, wall clock, allocation, IO or scheduler is introduced.
Invalid C state/policy and null required inputs produce a nonempty fault and zero-initialized outputs. New C clock layout/contract version is explicit; old torque ABI layout is preserved.

Clock composition replaces the precomputed cycle clock_fault with its own result before the existing final gate; allocation/guard validation retains existing priority. Every held final command must be exact zero.

planned_validation.clock_cases: Cartesian timestamp/previous/period/dt edges, including uint64 extrema, >2^53 exact millisecond values, malformed Python types and nextafter tolerance boundaries; seeded stateful sequences with gaps/backward/restarts/invalid dt.
planned_validation.oracle: Extract the Python source clock block without changing behavior; retain a frozen legacy implementation in tests and compare both. Compare C fault, normalized now and exact next clock state in the representable domain.
planned_validation.gate_composition: Compare C clock-plus-existing-gate against Python source-pipeline records, including original latch/clock regression sequences; clock faults must inhibit exact-zero final output.
planned_validation.abi_edges: All byte tags, invalid period bounds/state, UINT64_MAX subtraction, null pointers, no unsigned wrap, initialized outputs and explicit out-of-domain adapter rejection.
planned_validation.determinism: Repeat source-hashed finite compiled experiment with identical results; preserve prior receipts and PR heads.
planned_validation.review: Independent practical source review and bounded adversarial probes before draft PR.
planned_validation.ci: Run reference regressions and compiled parity on supported Python versions and GCC/Clang, including standalone ASAN/UBSan probe.

excluded_claims: No native allocator, pedal trust/latch, slew policy or complete pipeline port.
No raw MCU counter wrap normalization, target oscillator drift, scheduler jitter, input freshness/capture provenance or calibrated signal mapping.
No firmware flash, CAN, motor enable, HIL, WCET/memory budget, controls-team approval or safety certification.
